status: unaccepted source-anchored authored fringe approximation; overlay and sampling review pending
source: Katsushika Hokusai, Under the Wave off Kanagawa, Met JP1847, DP130155
method: Manual closed cubic contours authored from visual inspection of the unmodified canonical scan and baseline/reference-crop.png. No thresholding, flood fill, image generation or automatic tracing.
purpose: One connected parent on the right-hand crest arm with three unequal attached subordinate fingers. Bounded reference study only; not a whole-wave stamp or procedural motif.

landmarks.role: Approximate attachment transect inside the pale right-hand arm, below its upper skyline; the cut edge is an authored ROI boundary, not a printed foam boundary.
Upper right-turning subordinate tip; shorter reach and higher return than the lower group. Position and curvature need source overlay confirmation.
Intermediate scalloped projection on the descending arm; the inner dark contour is treated separately from foam.
Longer outer-right projection with a downward return. Approximate landmark rather than a measured exact contour.
Lower returning tip on the diagonal parent; terminal boundary is simplified and requires overlay review.

assumptions: Positive paths overlap at broad roots to author a connected foam network; sampled connectivity has not been checked.
Three unequal subordinate contours follow the descending right-hand-arm flow. Small scallops, fine ink irregularities and detached spray are omitted.
Subtract paths approximate strong interior ink contours and narrow dark gaps; an interior dark mark is not assumed to be exterior-connected water.
Pale paper outside the authored positive paths is negative space. The arbitrary parent attachment transect is documented rather than presented as a traced boundary.
Shared roots target at least roughly 4-6 normalized units before sampling, but no minimum sampled width or phase robustness is claimed.
Boundary locations and landmark matches are visual estimates. No source-overlay confirmation or accurate-trace claim is made.
The accepted interior calibration fragment does not transfer acceptance to this new fringe.
